You are working in the Go repository github.com/gin-gonic/gin checked out at /gin (gin v1.8.1). A bug was injected into the file /gin/context.go. A hidden test named TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment (in package gin, file context_test.go) is expected to pass once the bug is fixed; that exact checking version of the test is NOT in the repository (the in-repo tests currently all pass and must NOT be modified). Your job: find the injected bug in /gin/context.go and fix it with a minimal edit.

Method suggestions: the test name suggests it is about rendering a file/attachment and escaping. Look at Context.FileAttachment, Context.File, Context.FileFromFS, Context.Attachment, and the helper that builds the Content-Disposition header (e.g. func (c *Context) FileAttachment(filepath, filename string) or an internal helper like `func (c *Context) FileAttachment(...)`/`escapeQuotes`). In upstream gin, Context.FileAttachment calls `c.FileAttachment` -> `c.Writer.Header().Set("Content-Disposition", contentDisposition(filename))` where contentDisposition escapes quotes/backslashes; a bug could be that the filename is not escaped (quotes not escaped) or that the escaping is wrong. Write your own throwaway test file (e.g. /gin/zz_file_probe_test.go) that calls the relevant function with a filename containing a double quote and a backslash and checks the resulting Content-Disposition header (expected upstream behavior: `attachment; filename="a\"b"` style escaping, i.e. the quote is escaped with a backslash). IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS: do not modify or delete any pre-existing test file; do not break any pre-existing test (run `cd /gin && go test ./...` at the end and make sure everything still passes); no new features; minimal change in context.go only. You are working in the Go repository github.com/gin-gonic/gin checked out at /gin (gin v1.8.1). A bug was injected into the file /gin/tree.go. A hidden test named TestRouteParamsNotEmpty (in package gin, file tree_test.go) is expected to pass once the bug is fixed; that exact checking version of the test is NOT in the repository (the in-repo tests currently all pass and must NOT be modified). Your job: find the injected bug in /gin/tree.go and fix it with a minimal edit.

Context already gathered: the tree is a radix tree (httprouter-derived). getValue() saves params into the caller-provided *Params slice (only when `params != nil && cap(*params) > 0`), and rolls back to skippedNodes on backtracking. A brute-force search over random route sets with fresh Params/skippedNodes did NOT find any case where a matched route with wildcards returned empty params, so the bug is probably in a less common path: e.g. (1) reusing the SAME params/skippedNodes slices across several getValue calls (as the gin Context does across requests, including a first request that fails/backtracks and a second that matches), (2) trailing-slash / TSR lookups, (3) unescape=true, (4) routes with catch-all (`*filepath`) combined with params, (5) the `skippedNode.paramsCount` rollback truncating the params slice too far (e.g. `*value.params = (*value.params)[:skippedNode.paramsCount]`), (6) the `globalParamsCount` bookkeeping. Write throwaway tests (e.g. /gin/zz_tree_probe_test.go) that reuse one Params and one skippedNodes slice across many getValue calls (mimicking a live server: request A that backtracks, then request B that should match with params) and assert that when value.handlers != nil and the matched fullPath contains ':' or '*', the returned params are non-empty and have the right keys/values. Also compare against what the repo's own test helper checkRequests expects. IMPORTANT CONSTRAINTS: do not modify or delete any pre-existing test file; do not break any pre-existing test (run `cd /gin && go test ./...` at the end and make sure everything still passes); no new features; minimal change in tree.go only. NOTE: another agent is concurrently editing the function findCaseInsensitivePathRec in the same file, so do not touch findCaseInsensitivePathRec / findCaseInsensitivePath / shiftNRuneBytes; only work on addRoute/insertChild/getValue/addChild/params logic. Delete any throwaway test files you created before finishing. Report back: the exact diff you applied, the reasoning, and the test output proving all tests pass.
